forbids: any state, key, token or chip that says a requirement is met, covered, satisfied or compliant because a policy maps to it
note: The rule the skill exists to hold. Adding a `covered` column is a one-line change nothing else in the codebase would object to, and the result is a register asserting the most common quiet untruth in this industry — that having a policy means the thing is controlled. Both halves are needed: the static scan cannot see a state assembled at runtime, and the behavioural scan cannot see a field computed for a caller that does not exist yet.

mutations.why: a coverage field declared in shipped code under a name that gives nothing away, even if no output ever carries it. This is how it actually arrives: a helper is written for a caller that lands two releases later.
defeats: no shipped .py names, assigns or holds a coverage verdict

mutations.why: the same claim assembled at RUNTIME from fragments no word list can match. The static AST scan reads string literals and sees only 'cov' and 'ered'; the assigned key is the innocent `state`. This is exactly why the behavioural half has to exist and be proved separately.
defeats: no key or status in the analysis says a requirement is met
no chip on the rendered page carries a coverage verdict
